title: Invisible
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Aya Kinomiya grows up in a family where her father beats her mother and controls the household, her older brother looks away, and her mother silently endures for the children's sake. After a violent quarrel, Aya wishes she were not there and gains the power to turn invisible; she enjoys it at first, then makes a choice she may blame herself for all her life. A four-volume psychological drama about reclaiming normal life and facing pain.
life_message: Escaping pain is not the same as healing; one has to face what happened and live on.

Fifth-commandment failure of a father shown truthfully.
Concern for the oppressed in the home.
Attention to victims of domestic violence.
Injustice of a cruel father; mother's patience.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Abuse is shown as harm, not as family honor (MangaUpdates blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Aya seeks escape from a controlling father.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Mother endures for the children; family at the center.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Reclaiming normal life and her own pain (publisher blurb).

folkways.japan: Reflects the Japanese pattern of keeping family trouble hidden (sekentei) and a mother's silent endurance (gaman).

delivery.evidence: No review could be retrieved (to verify); themes carried by Aya's choice and its aftermath.
delivery.note: The abusive father is a source of harm in the summaries, not a voice for an argued worldview.

winners_losers: Aya survives and grows up carrying guilt; the abusive father is the source of harm; sympathy goes to Aya and her mother.
